title: Gluing finite-presentation modifications at finitely many closed points
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ be distinct closed points, with $r\geq0$. Set $U=S\setminus\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}$, $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s_i}$, and $V_i=S_i\setminus\{s_i\}$. Let $\mathcal C(S,U)$ be the category whose objects are morphisms $X\to S$ of finite presentation inducing isomorphisms $X\times_SU\to U$, and whose arrows are $S$-morphisms; define $\mathcal C(S_i,V_i)$ in the same way [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-fibre-product]. Here finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The base-change functor
$$\mathcal C(S,U)\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal C(S_i,V_i)$$
is an equivalence of categories: every family of local objects is induced by a global object, and every family of arrows between their restrictions lifts to exactly one global arrow. For $X\in\mathcal C(S,U)$, the morphism $X\to S$ is proper if and only if every $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every arrow $a:X\to X'$ in $\mathcal C(S,U)$, each of the properties proper, finite, and integral holds for $a$ if and only if it holds for every $a\times_SS_i$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For $r=0$, the product category is the terminal category and the assertions have their usual empty-family meanings.
